+# The Daily Grind
+
+The homepage loads `analytics.js` with a deferred script. Configure its
+`data-endpoint` in `index.html` to point to your analytics receiver (default:
+`/api/analytics`). This static project does not provide a receiver; deployment
+must route that URL to a service that accepts JSON POST requests:
+
+```json
+{"events":[{"type":"page_view","timestamp":"2026-11-08T00:00:00.000Z","path":"/"},{"type":"click","timestamp":"2026-11-08T00:00:00.500Z","path":"/","target":"a","id":"","destination":"/menu"}]}
+```
+
+Events send after one second without activity, with a ten-second maximum wait.
+Batches are capped at 100 events and 48 KiB. A full batch is scheduled for
+immediate background delivery before a new batch starts. Native `fetchLater()`
+handles navigation; other browsers use low-priority, keepalive fetches on a timer,
+when the page becomes hidden, or on `pagehide`. Delivery is best effort, without
+retries or persistent storage. A native scheduling failure drops that batch.
+Click metadata excludes page text, input values, and URL queries/fragments.
+
+Run `npm test` for deterministic Node tests; no browser or server is required.

+# The Daily Grind
+
+A static coffee homepage with browser-encrypted delivery notes.
+
+## Build and checks
+
+Use `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm build`, and `pnpm test`.
+`assets/notes.js` is the committed browser bundle; rebuild after editing `src/`.
+The existing static hosting command remains unchanged. Serve over HTTPS (or localhost) for Web Crypto.
+
+## Delivery notes
+
+The default is an explicitly labeled **local demo**. It generates a recipient key in memory, encrypts notes, downloads JSON envelopes, and lets the user preview decryption. Nothing is uploaded or persisted. Reloading closes access to the demo key, so downloaded demo files cannot subsequently be recovered. The application clears the input after successful encryption; Clear removes the envelope and any visible plaintext. JavaScript strings cannot be reliably zeroed, and client encryption does not protect against compromised same-origin scripts or browser extensions.
+
+The protocol uses noble's MLKEM768-X25519 hybrid KEM, HKDF-SHA256 with a fresh 32-byte salt and protocol context, and Web Crypto AES-256-GCM with a fresh 12-byte IV and 128-bit authentication tag. Each note has a new capsule, salt, IV and ID. Version, suite, recipient ID, and note ID are authenticated as AAD. Raw shared-secret buffers and encoded plaintext buffers are zeroed after use. The browser bundle includes the pinned cryptographic implementation, with no runtime crypto CDN dependency.
+
+## Configure a real recipient
+
+1. Generate an MLKEM768-X25519 key pair in the delivery team's trusted environment using the pinned library. Keep its secret key outside this site.
+2. Authenticate the 1216-byte public key through a trusted channel. Set `deliveryRecipient` in `src/recipient.js` to `{ id: 'delivery-key-2026-01', publicKey: '<base64 public key>' }` and rebuild. This pins the key in the deployed application. Retain old recipient secrets for key rotation and existing envelopes.
+3. In configured mode, the local decryption preview is hidden. Customers can download a file encrypted solely for that recipient. Integrate an authenticated order API to actually attach an envelope to an order; this static project has no order backend and does not claim notes have been delivered.
+4. The recipient can call `openNote(envelope, { id, secretKey })` from `src/crypto.js` in a trusted process. Never distribute the secret key with this website. The recipient and note IDs in the envelope are public; place sensitive instructions only inside the encrypted note.
+
+Cryptography reference: https://github.com/paulmillr/noble-post-quantum

+import { ml_kem768_x25519 as hybrid } from '@noble/post-quantum/hybrid.js';
+
+export const SUITE = 'MLKEM768-X25519/HKDF-SHA256/AES-256-GCM';
+const encoder = new TextEncoder();
+export const toBase64 = bytes => btoa(String.fromCharCode(...bytes));
+export function fromBase64(value) {
+  if (typeof value !== 'string' || value.length > 16384) throw new Error('Invalid envelope encoding.');
+  return Uint8Array.from(atob(value), c => c.charCodeAt(0));
+}
+export function createDemoRecipient() {
+  const keys = hybrid.keygen();
+  return { id: 'local-demo', ...keys };
+}
+function metadata(envelope) {
+  return encoder.encode(JSON.stringify({ version: envelope.version, suite: envelope.suite, recipient: envelope.recipient, id: envelope.id }));
+}
+async function deriveKey(secret, salt, context, usage) {
+  try {
+    const material = await crypto.subtle.importKey('raw', secret, 'HKDF', false, ['deriveKey']);
+    return await crypto.subtle.deriveKey({ name: 'HKDF', hash: 'SHA-256', salt, info: context }, material,
+      { name: 'AES-GCM', length: 256 }, false, [usage]);
+  } finally {
+    secret.fill(0);
+  }
+}
+export async function sealNote(note, recipient) {
+  if (!note.trim() || note.length > 1000) throw new Error('Enter a note of 1–1,000 characters.');
+  if (!(recipient.publicKey instanceof Uint8Array) || recipient.publicKey.length !== 1216) throw new Error('Invalid delivery recipient key.');
+  const { cipherText, sharedSecret } = hybrid.encapsulate(recipient.publicKey);
+  const envelope = { version: 1, suite: SUITE, recipient: recipient.id, id: crypto.randomUUID() };
+  const context = metadata(envelope);
+  const salt = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(32));
+  const iv = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(12));
+  const key = await deriveKey(sharedSecret, salt, context, 'encrypt');
+  const plaintext = encoder.encode(note);
+  try {
+    const ciphertext = await crypto.subtle.encrypt({ name: 'AES-GCM', iv, additionalData: context, tagLength: 128 }, key, plaintext);
+    return { ...envelope, capsule: toBase64(cipherText), salt: toBase64(salt), iv: toBase64(iv), ciphertext: toBase64(new Uint8Array(ciphertext)) };
+  } finally {
+    plaintext.fill(0);
+  }
+}
+export async function openNote(envelope, recipient) {
+  if (envelope.version !== 1 || envelope.suite !== SUITE || envelope.recipient !== recipient.id || typeof envelope.id !== 'string') throw new Error('Invalid envelope metadata.');
+  const capsule = fromBase64(envelope.capsule);
+  const salt = fromBase64(envelope.salt);
+  const iv = fromBase64(envelope.iv);
+  if (capsule.length !== 1120 || salt.length !== 32 || iv.length !== 12) throw new Error('Invalid envelope parameters.');
+  const context = metadata(envelope);
+  const secret = hybrid.decapsulate(capsule, recipient.secretKey);
+  const key = await deriveKey(secret, salt, context, 'decrypt');
+  const plaintext = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.decrypt({ name: 'AES-GCM', iv, additionalData: context, tagLength: 128 }, key, fromBase64(envelope.ciphertext)));
+  try { return new TextDecoder('utf-8', { fatal: true }).decode(plaintext); }
+  finally { plaintext.fill(0); }
+}

+import { test } from 'node:test';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { createDemoRecipient, sealNote, openNote, fromBase64, toBase64 } from '../src/crypto.js';
+
+test('hybrid envelope recovers Unicode notes using only the recipient key', async () => {
+  const recipient = createDemoRecipient();
+  try {
+    const note = 'Side gate code: 0421. Please don’t ring. ☕ مرحباً';
+    const envelope = await sealNote(note, { id: recipient.id, publicKey: recipient.publicKey });
+    assert.equal(await openNote(envelope, recipient), note);
+    assert.equal(fromBase64(envelope.iv).length, 12);
+    assert.equal(fromBase64(envelope.capsule).length, 1120);
+    assert.ok(!JSON.stringify(envelope).includes('0421'));
+    assert.ok(!('secretKey' in envelope));
+    const second = await sealNote(note, recipient);
+    assert.notEqual(second.iv, envelope.iv);
+    assert.notEqual(second.capsule, envelope.capsule);
+    assert.notEqual(second.ciphertext, envelope.ciphertext);
+  } finally { recipient.secretKey.fill(0); }
+});
+
+test('AEAD rejects modified ciphertext, capsule, IV, salt and authenticated metadata', async () => {
+  const recipient = createDemoRecipient();
+  try {
+    const envelope = await sealNote('Please use the side gate.', recipient);
+    for (const field of ['ciphertext', 'capsule', 'iv', 'salt']) {
+      const bytes = fromBase64(envelope[field]);
+      bytes[0] ^= 1;
+      await assert.rejects(openNote({ ...envelope, [field]: toBase64(bytes) }, recipient));
+    }
+    await assert.rejects(openNote({ ...envelope, id: 'different-order' }, recipient));
+    await assert.rejects(openNote({ ...envelope, recipient: 'someone-else' }, recipient));
+    await assert.rejects(openNote({ ...envelope, version: 2 }, recipient));
+    await assert.rejects(openNote({ ...envelope, suite: 'AES-GCM' }, recipient));
+    const wrongRecipient = createDemoRecipient();
+    try { await assert.rejects(openNote(envelope, wrongRecipient)); }
+    finally { wrongRecipient.secretKey.fill(0); }
+  } finally { recipient.secretKey.fill(0); }
+});
+
+test('rejects blank and oversized notes, invalid recipients and malformed envelopes', async () => {
+  const recipient = createDemoRecipient();
+  try {
+    await assert.rejects(sealNote('  ', recipient));
+    await assert.rejects(sealNote('x'.repeat(1001), recipient));
+    await assert.rejects(sealNote('hello', { id: 'bad', publicKey: new Uint8Array(32) }));
+    const envelope = await sealNote('hello', recipient);
+    await assert.rejects(openNote({ ...envelope, iv: 'AA==' }, recipient));
+    await assert.rejects(openNote({ ...envelope, ciphertext: '!bad base64!' }, recipient));
+  } finally { recipient.secretKey.fill(0); }
+});

-# The DevTools Times
+# smallpt playground
 
-This project is a sample news application built with Astro, designed to serve as a testing ground for new features in Chrome DevTools.
+Kevin Beason’s original C++ smallpt path tracer, compiled to WebAssembly and
+rendered entirely in the browser. The home page builds to `dist/client/index.html`.
+Its preview is also a real render made by the same compiled Wasm module.
 
+## Build
+
+Requires Node.js, pnpm, and Emscripten (`em++` on PATH).
 
 ```sh
-pnpm install && pnpm run start
+pnpm install
+pnpm build
 ```
 
-The application will now be running on `http://localhost:11224`.
+The build first recompiles C++ using `scripts/build-wasm.sh`, then builds Astro.
+The checked-in `public/wasm/smallpt.js` and `smallpt.wasm` are the browser assets.
+The page is prerendered and its HTML, `_astro` assets, fonts, preview, and `wasm`
+directory can be served as static files from `dist/client`. Other existing app
+routes retain their original server rendering configuration.

+change the walls’ and spheres’ colors, adjust samples/resolution to rerender,

diff --git a/public/wasm/render-worker.js b/public/wasm/render-worker.js
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..b8f33a3
--- /dev/null
+++ b/public/wasm/render-worker.js
@@ -0,0 +1,63 @@
+import initSmallpt from "./smallpt.js";
+
+let renderer;
+self.onmessage = async ({ data }) => {
+  try {
+    const { width, height, samples, seed, randomize } = data;
+    if (
+      ![480, 640, 800, 1024].includes(width) ||
+      height !== (width * 3) / 4 ||
+      ![16, 64, 128, 256].includes(samples)
+    ) {
+      throw new Error("Invalid render settings.");
+    }
+    renderer ??= await initSmallpt();
+    const pointer = renderer._begin_render(
+      width,
+      height,
+      samples,
+      seed,
+      Number(randomize),
+    );
+    if (!pointer)
+      throw new Error(
+        "Unable to allocate render memory. Try a smaller resolution.",
+      );
+    const colors = [0, 1, 6, 7].map((id) => ({
+      id,
+      hex: `#${renderer._scene_color(id).toString(16).padStart(6, "0")}`,
+    }));
+    self.postMessage({ type: "started", colors });
+    const started = performance.now();
+    for (let row = 0; row < height; row += 4) {
+      const count = Math.min(4, height - row);
+      renderer._render_rows(row, count);
+      // Copy only newly rendered rows. Transfer ownership to avoid copying again.
+      const offset = pointer + row * width * 4;
+      const pixels = new Uint8ClampedArray(
+        renderer.HEAPU8.buffer,
+        offset,
+        width * count * 4,
+      ).slice();
+      self.postMessage(
+        {
+          type: "rows",
+          pixels,
+          row,
+          count,
+          width,
+          height,
+          progress: (row + count) / height,
+          elapsed: performance.now() - started,
+        },
+        [pixels.buffer],
+      );
+    }
+    self.postMessage({ type: "done", elapsed: performance.now() - started });
+  } catch (error) {
+    self.postMessage({
+      type: "error",
+      message: error instanceof Error ? error.message : "Rendering failed.",
+    });
+  }
+};

+#include <math.h>   // smallpt, a Path Tracer by Kevin Beason, 2008
+#include <stdlib.h> // Make : g++ -O3 -fopenmp smallpt.cpp -o smallpt
+#include <stdio.h>  //        Remove "-fopenmp" for g++ version < 4.2
+struct Vec {        // Usage: time ./smallpt 5000 && xv image.ppm
+  double x, y, z;                  // position, also color (r,g,b)
+  Vec(double x_=0, double y_=0, double z_=0){ x=x_; y=y_; z=z_; }
+  Vec operator+(const Vec &b) const { return Vec(x+b.x,y+b.y,z+b.z); }
+  Vec operator-(const Vec &b) const { return Vec(x-b.x,y-b.y,z-b.z); }
+  Vec operator*(double b) const { return Vec(x*b,y*b,z*b); }
+  Vec mult(const Vec &b) const { return Vec(x*b.x,y*b.y,z*b.z); }
+  Vec& norm(){ return *this = *this * (1/sqrt(x*x+y*y+z*z)); }
+  double dot(const Vec &b) const { return x*b.x+y*b.y+z*b.z; } // cross:
+  Vec operator%(Vec&b){return Vec(y*b.z-z*b.y,z*b.x-x*b.z,x*b.y-y*b.x);}
+};
+struct Ray { Vec o, d; Ray(Vec o_, Vec d_) : o(o_), d(d_) {} };
+enum Refl_t { DIFF, SPEC, REFR };  // material types, used in radiance()
+struct Sphere {
+  double rad;       // radius
+  Vec p, e, c;      // position, emission, color
+  Refl_t refl;      // reflection type (DIFFuse, SPECular, REFRactive)
+  Sphere(double rad_, Vec p_, Vec e_, Vec c_, Refl_t refl_):
+    rad(rad_), p(p_), e(e_), c(c_), refl(refl_) {}
+  double intersect(const Ray &r) const { // returns distance, 0 if nohit
+    Vec op = p-r.o; // Solve t^2*d.d + 2*t*(o-p).d + (o-p).(o-p)-R^2 = 0
+    double t, eps=1e-4, b=op.dot(r.d), det=b*b-op.dot(op)+rad*rad;
+    if (det<0) return 0; else det=sqrt(det);
+    return (t=b-det)>eps ? t : ((t=b+det)>eps ? t : 0);
+  }
+};
+Sphere spheres[] = {//Scene: radius, position, emission, color, material
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec( 1e5+1,40.8,81.6), Vec(),Vec(.75,.25,.25),DIFF),//Left
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(-1e5+99,40.8,81.6),Vec(),Vec(.25,.25,.75),DIFF),//Rght
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(50,40.8, 1e5),     Vec(),Vec(.75,.75,.75),DIFF),//Back
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(50,40.8,-1e5+170), Vec(),Vec(),           DIFF),//Frnt
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(50, 1e5, 81.6),    Vec(),Vec(.75,.75,.75),DIFF),//Botm
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(50,-1e5+81.6,81.6),Vec(),Vec(.75,.75,.75),DIFF),//Top
+  Sphere(16.5,Vec(27,16.5,47),       Vec(),Vec(1,1,1)*.999, SPEC),//Mirr
+  Sphere(16.5,Vec(73,16.5,78),       Vec(),Vec(1,1,1)*.999, REFR),//Glas
+  Sphere(600, Vec(50,681.6-.27,81.6),Vec(12,12,12),  Vec(), DIFF) //Lite
+};
+inline double clamp(double x){ return x<0 ? 0 : x>1 ? 1 : x; }
+inline int toInt(double x){ return int(pow(clamp(x),1/2.2)*255+.5); }
+inline bool intersect(const Ray &r, double &t, int &id){
+  double n=sizeof(spheres)/sizeof(Sphere), d, inf=t=1e20;
+  for(int i=int(n);i--;) if((d=spheres[i].intersect(r))&&d<t){t=d;id=i;}
+  return t<inf;

+Vec radiance(const Ray &r, int depth, unsigned short *Xi){
+  double t;                               // distance to intersection
+  int id=0;                               // id of intersected object
+  if (!intersect(r, t, id)) return Vec(); // if miss, return black
+  const Sphere &obj = spheres[id];        // the hit object
+  Vec x=r.o+r.d*t, n=(x-obj.p).norm(), nl=n.dot(r.d)<0?n:n*-1, f=obj.c;
+  double p = f.x>f.y && f.x>f.z ? f.x : f.y>f.z ? f.y : f.z; // max refl
+  if (++depth>5) if (erand48(Xi)<p) f=f*(1/p); else return obj.e; //R.R.
+  if (obj.refl == DIFF){                  // Ideal DIFFUSE reflection
+    double r1=2*M_PI*erand48(Xi), r2=erand48(Xi), r2s=sqrt(r2);
+    Vec w=nl, u=((fabs(w.x)>.1?Vec(0,1):Vec(1))%w).norm(), v=w%u;
+    Vec d = (u*cos(r1)*r2s + v*sin(r1)*r2s + w*sqrt(1-r2)).norm();

+  } else if (obj.refl == SPEC)            // Ideal SPECULAR reflection
+    return obj.e + f.mult(radiance(Ray(x,r.d-n*2*n.dot(r.d)),depth,Xi));

+  bool into = n.dot(nl)>0;                // Ray from outside going in?
+  double nc=1, nt=1.5, nnt=into?nc/nt:nt/nc, ddn=r.d.dot(nl), cos2t;
+  if ((cos2t=1-nnt*nnt*(1-ddn*ddn))<0)    // Total internal reflection

+  return obj.e + f.mult(depth>2 ? (erand48(Xi)<P ?   // Russian roulette
+    radiance(reflRay,depth,Xi)*RP:radiance(Ray(x,tdir),depth,Xi)*TP) :
+    radiance(reflRay,depth,Xi)*Re+radiance(Ray(x,tdir),depth,Xi)*Tr);
+}
+int main(int argc, char *argv[]){
+  int w=1024, h=768, samps = argc==2 ? atoi(argv[1])/4 : 1; // # samples
+  Ray cam(Vec(50,52,295.6), Vec(0,-0.042612,-1).norm()); // cam pos, dir
+  Vec cx=Vec(w*.5135/h), cy=(cx%cam.d).norm()*.5135, r, *c=new Vec[w*h];
+#pragma omp parallel for schedule(dynamic, 1) private(r)       // OpenMP
+  for (int y=0; y<h; y++){                       // Loop over image rows
+    fprintf(stderr,"\rRendering (%d spp) %5.2f%%",samps*4,100.*y/(h-1));
+    for (unsigned short x=0, Xi[3]={0,0,y*y*y}; x<w; x++)   // Loop cols
+      for (int sy=0, i=(h-y-1)*w+x; sy<2; sy++)     // 2x2 subpixel rows

@@ -0,0 +1,20 @@
+# smallpt WebAssembly port
+
+The source is Kevin Beason’s MIT-licensed smallpt (2008), downloaded from
+https://www.kevinbeason.com/smallpt/smallpt.txt. `smallpt.original.cpp` is the
+unmodified 99-line original; `LICENSE.txt` retains the upstream license.
+
+`smallpt.cpp` retains the original scene, sphere intersections, camera model,
+Monte Carlo radiance integrator, diffuse/specular/refractive materials,
+Russian roulette, tent-filtered 2×2 subpixels, and gamma correction. The original
+PPM-writing `main` and OpenMP loop are replaced by a small C interface:
+
+- `begin_render`: allocate an RGBA image, restore the original scene, and
+  optionally assign seeded random colors to the two walls and both spheres.
+- `render_rows`: render a batch of rows into that image.
+- `scene_color`: return the scene’s actual display-space material colors.
+
+The module runs in a dedicated module Worker. Each completed row batch is sent
+as a transferable buffer to the main thread, which draws it on a canvas. A new
+render terminates the previous worker, so restarting never queues old work.
+No SharedArrayBuffer or cross-origin isolation headers are required.

+// Browser adaptation of smallpt by Kevin Beason. See LICENSE.txt.
+#include <math.h>   // smallpt, a Path Tracer by Kevin Beason, 2008
+#include <stdlib.h> // Make : g++ -O3 -fopenmp smallpt.cpp -o smallpt
+#include <stdio.h>  //        Remove "-fopenmp" for g++ version < 4.2
+struct Vec {        // Usage: time ./smallpt 5000 && xv image.ppm
+  double x, y, z;                  // position, also color (r,g,b)
+  Vec(double x_=0, double y_=0, double z_=0){ x=x_; y=y_; z=z_; }
+  Vec operator+(const Vec &b) const { return Vec(x+b.x,y+b.y,z+b.z); }
+  Vec operator-(const Vec &b) const { return Vec(x-b.x,y-b.y,z-b.z); }
+  Vec operator*(double b) const { return Vec(x*b,y*b,z*b); }
+  Vec mult(const Vec &b) const { return Vec(x*b.x,y*b.y,z*b.z); }
+  Vec& norm(){ return *this = *this * (1/sqrt(x*x+y*y+z*z)); }
+  double dot(const Vec &b) const { return x*b.x+y*b.y+z*b.z; } // cross:
+  Vec operator%(Vec&b){return Vec(y*b.z-z*b.y,z*b.x-x*b.z,x*b.y-y*b.x);}
+};
+struct Ray { Vec o, d; Ray(Vec o_, Vec d_) : o(o_), d(d_) {} };
+enum Refl_t { DIFF, SPEC, REFR };  // material types, used in radiance()
+struct Sphere {
+  double rad;       // radius
+  Vec p, e, c;      // position, emission, color
+  Refl_t refl;      // reflection type (DIFFuse, SPECular, REFRactive)
+  Sphere(double rad_, Vec p_, Vec e_, Vec c_, Refl_t refl_):
+    rad(rad_), p(p_), e(e_), c(c_), refl(refl_) {}
+  double intersect(const Ray &r) const { // returns distance, 0 if nohit
+    Vec op = p-r.o; // Solve t^2*d.d + 2*t*(o-p).d + (o-p).(o-p)-R^2 = 0
+    double t, eps=1e-4, b=op.dot(r.d), det=b*b-op.dot(op)+rad*rad;
+    if (det<0) return 0; else det=sqrt(det);
+    return (t=b-det)>eps ? t : ((t=b+det)>eps ? t : 0);
+  }
+};
+Sphere spheres[] = {//Scene: radius, position, emission, color, material
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec( 1e5+1,40.8,81.6), Vec(),Vec(.75,.25,.25),DIFF),//Left
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(-1e5+99,40.8,81.6),Vec(),Vec(.25,.25,.75),DIFF),//Rght
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(50,40.8, 1e5),     Vec(),Vec(.75,.75,.75),DIFF),//Back
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(50,40.8,-1e5+170), Vec(),Vec(),           DIFF),//Frnt
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(50, 1e5, 81.6),    Vec(),Vec(.75,.75,.75),DIFF),//Botm
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(50,-1e5+81.6,81.6),Vec(),Vec(.75,.75,.75),DIFF),//Top
+  Sphere(16.5,Vec(27,16.5,47),       Vec(),Vec(1,1,1)*.999, SPEC),//Mirr
+  Sphere(16.5,Vec(73,16.5,78),       Vec(),Vec(1,1,1)*.999, REFR),//Glas
+  Sphere(600, Vec(50,681.6-.27,81.6),Vec(12,12,12),  Vec(), DIFF) //Lite
+};

+  double n=sizeof(spheres)/sizeof(Sphere), d, inf=t=1e20;
+  for(int i=int(n);i--;) if((d=spheres[i].intersect(r))&&d<t){t=d;id=i;}
+  return t<inf;

+  double t;                               // distance to intersection
+  int id=0;                               // id of intersected object
+  if (!intersect(r, t, id)) return Vec(); // if miss, return black
+  const Sphere &obj = spheres[id];        // the hit object
+  Vec x=r.o+r.d*t, n=(x-obj.p).norm(), nl=n.dot(r.d)<0?n:n*-1, f=obj.c;
+  double p = f.x>f.y && f.x>f.z ? f.x : f.y>f.z ? f.y : f.z; // max refl
+  if (++depth>5) { if (erand48(Xi)<p) f=f*(1/p); else return obj.e; } //R.R.
+  if (obj.refl == DIFF){                  // Ideal DIFFUSE reflection
+    double r1=2*M_PI*erand48(Xi), r2=erand48(Xi), r2s=sqrt(r2);
+    Vec w=nl, u=((fabs(w.x)>.1?Vec(0,1):Vec(1))%w).norm(), v=w%u;
+    Vec d = (u*cos(r1)*r2s + v*sin(r1)*r2s + w*sqrt(1-r2)).norm();
+    return obj.e + f.mult(radiance(Ray(x,d),depth,Xi));
+  } else if (obj.refl == SPEC)            // Ideal SPECULAR reflection
+    return obj.e + f.mult(radiance(Ray(x,r.d-n*2*n.dot(r.d)),depth,Xi));
+  Ray reflRay(x, r.d-n*2*n.dot(r.d));     // Ideal dielectric REFRACTION
+  bool into = n.dot(nl)>0;                // Ray from outside going in?
+  double nc=1, nt=1.5, nnt=into?nc/nt:nt/nc, ddn=r.d.dot(nl), cos2t;
+  if ((cos2t=1-nnt*nnt*(1-ddn*ddn))<0)    // Total internal reflection

+    radiance(reflRay,depth,Xi)*RP:radiance(Ray(x,tdir),depth,Xi)*TP) :
+    radiance(reflRay,depth,Xi)*Re+radiance(Ray(x,tdir),depth,Xi)*Tr);

+
+// The original radiance integrator above is unchanged apart from explicit braces.
+// Browser adaptation: seeded colors and rows of RGBA pixels instead of a PPM file.
+#include <stdint.h>
+#include <initializer_list>
+static unsigned char *pixels = nullptr;
+static int width, height, samples;
+static uint32_t sceneSeed;
+static uint32_t rng;
+static double randomColor() {
+  rng ^= rng << 13; rng ^= rng >> 17; rng ^= rng << 5;
+  return .35 + .60 * (rng / 4294967295.0);
+}
+extern "C" {
+unsigned char *begin_render(int w, int h, int spp, uint32_t seed, int randomize) {
+  if (w < 1 || h < 1 || w > 2048 || h > 1536 || spp < 4 || spp > 4096) return nullptr;
+  free(pixels);
+  width = w; height = h; samples = spp / 4; sceneSeed = seed;
+  pixels = (unsigned char *)calloc((size_t)w*h*4, 1);
+  if (!pixels) return nullptr;
+  for (int i=0; i<w*h; i++) pixels[i*4+3] = 255;
+  spheres[0].c = Vec(.75,.25,.25); spheres[1].c = Vec(.25,.25,.75);
+  spheres[6].c = spheres[7].c = Vec(.999,.999,.999);
+  if (randomize) {
+    rng = seed ? seed : 1;
+    for (int id : {0, 1, 6, 7}) {
+      double r = randomColor(), g = randomColor(), b = randomColor();
+      spheres[id].c = Vec(r,g,b);
+    }
+  }
+  return pixels;
+}
+int scene_color(int id) {
+  if (id < 0 || id > 8) return 0;
+  Vec c = spheres[id].c;
+  return (toInt(c.x)<<16) | (toInt(c.y)<<8) | toInt(c.z);
+}
+void render_rows(int start, int count) {
+  Ray cam(Vec(50,52,295.6), Vec(0,-0.042612,-1).norm());
+  Vec cx=Vec(width*.5135/height), cy=(cx%cam.d).norm()*.5135;
+  for (int row=start; row<start+count && row<height; row++) {
+    int y=height-row-1;
+    unsigned short Xi[3] = {(unsigned short)sceneSeed, (unsigned short)(sceneSeed>>16), (unsigned short)(y*y*y)};
+    for (int x=0; x<width; x++) {
+      Vec c;
+      for (int sy=0; sy<2; sy++) for (int sx=0; sx<2; sx++) {
+        Vec r;
+        for (int s=0; s<samples; s++) {
+          double r1=2*erand48(Xi), dx=r1<1 ? sqrt(r1)-1 : 1-sqrt(2-r1);
+          double r2=2*erand48(Xi), dy=r2<1 ? sqrt(r2)-1 : 1-sqrt(2-r2);
+          Vec d=cx*(((sx+.5+dx)/2+x)/width-.5)+cy*(((sy+.5+dy)/2+y)/height-.5)+cam.d;
+          r=r+radiance(Ray(cam.o+d*140,d.norm()),0,Xi)*(1./samples);
+        }
+        c=c+Vec(clamp(r.x),clamp(r.y),clamp(r.z))*.25;
+      }
+      int i=(row*width+x)*4;
+      pixels[i]=toInt(c.x); pixels[i+1]=toInt(c.y); pixels[i+2]=toInt(c.z);
+    }
+  }
+}
+}

+import assert from "node:assert/strict";
+import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
+import init from "../public/wasm/smallpt.js";
+const binary = await readFile(
+  new URL("../public/wasm/smallpt.wasm", import.meta.url),
+);
+assert.ok(
+  WebAssembly.validate(binary),
+  "The artifact must be valid WebAssembly",
+);
+globalThis.fetch = async () =>
+  new Response(binary, { headers: { "Content-Type": "application/wasm" } });
+const wasm = await init();
+const width = 64,
+  height = 48;
+function render(seed, randomize, batch = height) {
+  const pointer = wasm._begin_render(
+    width,
+    height,
+    16,
+    seed,
+    Number(randomize),
+  );
+  assert.ok(pointer, "Render buffer allocation");
+  const colors = [0, 1, 6, 7].map((id) => wasm._scene_color(id));
+  for (let row = 0; row < height; row += batch) wasm._render_rows(row, batch);
+  const pixels = Buffer.from(
+    wasm.HEAPU8.subarray(pointer, pointer + width * height * 4),
+  );
+  for (let i = 3; i < pixels.length; i += 4)
+    assert.equal(pixels[i], 255, "Opaque RGBA output");
+  assert.ok(
+    pixels.some((value, i) => i % 4 !== 3 && value > 100),
+    "The scene must contain lit pixels",
+  );
+  return { pixels, colors };
+}
+const original = render(0, false);
+assert.deepEqual(
+  render(0, false, 4),
+  original,
+  "Row batching must preserve the rendered image",
+);
+const randomized = render(12345, true);
+assert.notDeepEqual(
+  randomized.colors,
+  original.colors,
+  "Randomized materials must change",
+);
+assert.notDeepEqual(
+  randomized.pixels,
+  original.pixels,
+  "Randomized scene must change actual pixels",
+);
+assert.deepEqual(
+  render(12345, true),
+  randomized,
+  "A seed must reproduce the scene",
+);
+assert.notDeepEqual(
+  render(67890, true).pixels,
+  randomized.pixels,
+  "Different seeds must change the render",
+);
+assert.deepEqual(
+  render(0, false),
+  original,
+  "Reset must restore the original scene",
+);
+assert.equal(
+  wasm._begin_render(-1, 48, 16, 0, 0),
+  0,
+  "Invalid dimensions must be rejected",
+);
+console.log(
+  "Wasm checks passed: valid module, lit RGBA output, row batching, random colors, seeded pixels, reset, and bounds.",
+);
+
+// Exercise the actual worker message handler using local bytes, without a server.
+const messages = [];
+globalThis.self = { postMessage: (data) => messages.push(data) };
+await import("../public/wasm/render-worker.js");
+await self.onmessage({
+  data: { width: 480, height: 360, samples: 16, seed: 12345, randomize: true },
+});
+assert.equal(messages[0].type, "started");
+assert.equal(messages.filter((data) => data.type === "rows").length, 90);
+assert.equal(messages.at(-2).progress, 1);
+assert.equal(messages.at(-1).type, "done");
+await self.onmessage({ data: { width: -1 } });
+assert.equal(messages.at(-1).type, "error");
+console.log(
+  "Worker checks passed: palette, 90 transferable row batches, completion, and invalid-setting errors.",
+);

+const canvas = document.querySelector<HTMLCanvasElement>("#render-canvas")!;
+const context = canvas.getContext("2d")!;
+const preview = document.querySelector<HTMLImageElement>("#preview")!;
+const viewport = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#viewport")!;
+const sampleSelect = document.querySelector<HTMLSelectElement>("#samples")!;
+const resolutionSelect =
+  document.querySelector<HTMLSelectElement>("#resolution")!;
+const randomizeButton =
+  document.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>("#randomize")!;
+const randomizeLabel = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#randomize-label")!;
+const resetButton = document.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>("#reset")!;
+const saveButton = document.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>("#download")!;
+const state = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#render-state")!;
+const stateText = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#state-text")!;
+const message = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#render-message")!;
+const elapsed = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#elapsed")!;
+let worker: Worker | undefined;
+let complete = false;
+let busy = false;
+let randomized = false;
+let seed = 0;
+
+function setBusy(value: boolean) {
+  busy = value;
+  state.classList.toggle("is-rendering", value);
+  canvas.setAttribute("aria-busy", String(value));
+  saveButton.disabled = value;
+  // The primary action can restart a running render with another palette.
+  randomizeLabel.textContent = value
+    ? "Randomize & restart"
+    : "Randomize & render";
+}
+
+function formatTime(ms: number) {
+  return ms < 1000
+    ? `${(ms / 1000).toFixed(2)} s`
+    : `${(ms / 1000).toFixed(1)} s`;
+}
+
+function showError(details: string) {
+  worker?.terminate();
+  worker = undefined;
+  setBusy(false);
+  stateText.textContent = "Render interrupted";
+  message.textContent = `${details} Use the render button to try again.`;
+  saveButton.disabled = !complete;
+}
+
+function render(useRandomColors: boolean, newPalette = false) {
+  if (typeof WebAssembly === "undefined" || typeof Worker === "undefined") {
+    showError("This browser needs WebAssembly and Web Worker support.");
+    return;
+  }
+  worker?.terminate();
+  randomized = useRandomColors;
+  if (newPalette) seed = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint32Array(1))[0];
+  if (!useRandomColors) seed = 0;
+  const width = Number(resolutionSelect.value);
+  const height = (width * 3) / 4;
+  const samples = Number(sampleSelect.value);
+  // Retain the preceding image underneath the new rows while rendering.
+  if (complete) {
+    preview.src = canvas.toDataURL("image/png");
+    preview.alt =
+      "Previous path-traced scene, shown while the new render completes";
+  }
+  complete = false;
+  viewport.classList.remove("has-render");
+  canvas.width = width;
+  canvas.height = height;
+  setBusy(true);
+  stateText.textContent = "Starting renderer";
+  message.textContent = "Warming up a little world of light…";
+  elapsed.textContent = "0.0 s";
+  document.querySelector("#render-resolution")!.textContent =
+    `${width} × ${height}`;
+  document.querySelector("#render-samples")!.textContent =
+    `${samples} samples / pixel`;
+  try {
+    const activeWorker = new Worker("/wasm/render-worker.js", { type: "module" });
+    worker = activeWorker;
+    activeWorker.onerror = () => {
+      if (worker === activeWorker) {
+        showError("The renderer could not load. Check your connection and try again.");
+      }
+    };
+    activeWorker.onmessage = ({ data }) => {
+      if (worker !== activeWorker) return;
+      if (data.type === "started") {
+        document.querySelector("#palette-name")!.textContent = randomized
+          ? "Randomized"
+          : "Original";
+        for (const { id, hex } of data.colors) {
+          const swatch = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`#color-${id}`)!;
+          swatch.style.setProperty("--swatch", hex);
+          swatch.title = hex;
+        }
+        stateText.textContent = "Rendering · 0%";
+        message.textContent = "Following the light, one pixel at a time.";
+      } else if (data.type === "rows") {
+        context.putImageData(
+          new ImageData(data.pixels, data.width, data.count),
+          0,
+          data.row,
+        );
+        viewport.classList.add("has-render");
+        // Keep the preceding image visible in unfinished rows.
+        canvas.style.clipPath = `inset(0 0 ${100 - data.progress * 100}% 0)`;
+        stateText.textContent = `Rendering · ${Math.round(data.progress * 100)}%`;
+        elapsed.textContent = formatTime(data.elapsed);
+      } else if (data.type === "done") {
+        complete = true;
+        setBusy(false);
+        canvas.style.clipPath = "";
+        stateText.textContent = "Render complete";
+        message.textContent =
+          "A little light, a lot of possibility. Try another palette.";
+        elapsed.textContent = formatTime(data.elapsed);
+        worker?.terminate();
+        worker = undefined;
+      } else if (data.type === "error") {
+        showError(data.message);
+      }
+    };
+    worker.postMessage({
+      width,
+      height,
+      samples,
+      seed,
+      randomize: useRandomColors,
+    });
+  } catch (error) {
+    showError(
+      error instanceof Error ? error.message : "The renderer could not start.",
+    );
+  }
+}
+
+randomizeButton.addEventListener("click", () => render(true, true));
+resetButton.addEventListener("click", () => {
+  sampleSelect.value = "64";
+  resolutionSelect.value = "640";
+  render(false);
+});
+sampleSelect.addEventListener("change", () => render(randomized));
+resolutionSelect.addEventListener("change", () => render(randomized));
+saveButton.addEventListener("click", () => {
+  if (busy) return;
+  if (!complete) return;
+  canvas.toBlob((blob) => {
+    if (!blob) {
+      message.textContent = "The image could not be saved. Please try again.";
+      return;
+    }
+    const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
+    const link = document.createElement("a");
+    link.href = url;
+    link.download = `smallpt-${randomized ? seed : "original"}-${canvas.width}x${canvas.height}.png`;
+    link.click();
+    setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 1000);
+    message.textContent = "A little piece of light, saved as a PNG.";
+  }, "image/png");
+});
+window.addEventListener("pagehide", () => worker?.terminate());
+// The preview is an actual output of this same Wasm module. Start a fresh local
+// render automatically; the worker keeps the page interactive throughout.
+render(false);

-# The DevTools Times
+# smallpt — a little experiment in light
 
-This project is a sample news application built with Astro, designed to serve as a testing ground for new features in Chrome DevTools.
+Kevin Beason’s MIT-licensed smallpt C++ path tracer, compiled to WebAssembly with Emscripten. The home page is prerendered to `dist/client/index.html`. Rendering happens entirely in a dedicated browser worker, with progressive sample accumulation and no rendering service.
 
+- `pnpm install`
+- `pnpm run build` — build the site, using the checked-in WebAssembly artifacts.
+- `pnpm run build:wasm` — rebuild `public/wasm/smallpt.js` and `.wasm` with Emscripten (`em++` required).
+- `node scripts/check-wasm.mjs` — exercise the compiled renderer directly, without a browser or server.
 
-```sh
-pnpm install && pnpm run start
-```
+The canvas renders automatically at 640 × 480. Randomize changes both foreground sphere colors while keeping the original mirror/glass materials. Reset restores the original scene. Quality sets samples per pixel, and the download icon exports PNG. The initial image was rendered from the same C++ adaptation at 128 samples per pixel; live WebAssembly output replaces it after its first pass.
 
-The application will now be running on `http://localhost:11224`.
-
-## Tech Stack
-
-- **[Astro](https://astro.build/)**: The web framework for building content-driven websites.
-- **[React](https://react.dev/)**: Used for UI components.
-- **[Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/)**: For styling the application.
-- **[Astro DB](https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/database/)**: Powers the comments feature, using a libSQL-compatible database.
+Original source: https://www.kevinbeason.com/smallpt/ . Unmodified source and MIT license are preserved in `renderer/`. `renderer/smallpt.cpp` adapts the entry point for incremental rendering and adds a color interface. It retains smallpt’s ray/sphere intersections, recursive Monte Carlo radiance, Fresnel refraction, Russian roulette, and tent-filtered camera sampling. The browser adaptation averages unclamped radiance across passes, then applies the original gamma conversion for display.

+  double dot(const Vec &b) const { return x*b.x+y*b.y+z*b.z; } // cross:
+  Vec operator%(Vec&b){return Vec(y*b.z-z*b.y,z*b.x-x*b.z,x*b.y-y*b.x);}
+};

+  double rad;       // radius
+  Vec p, e, c;      // position, emission, color
+  Refl_t refl;      // reflection type (DIFFuse, SPECular, REFRactive)

+    rad(rad_), p(p_), e(e_), c(c_), refl(refl_) {}

+    Vec op = p-r.o; // Solve t^2*d.d + 2*t*(o-p).d + (o-p).(o-p)-R^2 = 0
+    double t, eps=1e-4, b=op.dot(r.d), det=b*b-op.dot(op)+rad*rad;
+    if (det<0) return 0; else det=sqrt(det);
+    return (t=b-det)>eps ? t : ((t=b+det)>eps ? t : 0);

+  Sphere(1e5, Vec( 1e5+1,40.8,81.6), Vec(),Vec(.75,.25,.25),DIFF),//Left
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(-1e5+99,40.8,81.6),Vec(),Vec(.25,.25,.75),DIFF),//Rght

+    return obj.e + f.mult(radiance(Ray(x,r.d-n*2*n.dot(r.d)),depth,Xi));

+  bool into = n.dot(nl)>0;                // Ray from outside going in?
+  double nc=1, nt=1.5, nnt=into?nc/nt:nt/nc, ddn=r.d.dot(nl), cos2t;

+      for(int sy=0;sy<2;sy++) for(int sx=0;sx<2;sx++) {
+        double r1=2*erand48(Xi), dx=r1<1?sqrt(r1)-1:1-sqrt(2-r1);

+    }

+#ifdef SMALLPT_NATIVE

+  for(int i=0;i<640*480;i++) fwrite(pixels.data()+i*4,1,3,f);
+  fclose(f);
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+set -euo pipefail
+cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
+mkdir -p public/wasm
+em++ renderer/smallpt.cpp -O3 --no-entry -s MODULARIZE=1 -s EXPORT_ES6=1 -s ENVIRONMENT=worker,node -s ALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH=1 -s STACK_SIZE=5242880 -s EXPORTED_RUNTIME_METHODS='["HEAPU8"]' -s EXPORTED_FUNCTIONS='["_init","_set_color","_buffer","_render_rows"]' -o public/wasm/smallpt.js

+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import createSmallpt from '../public/wasm/smallpt.js';
+const module = await createSmallpt();
+const width = 48, height = 36;
+function render(color) {
+  module._set_color(6, ...color);
+  module._set_color(7, ...color);
+  module._init(width, height, 42);
+  for(let pass=0;pass<4;pass++) for(let row=0;row<height;row+=6) module._render_rows(row, 6);
+  return module.HEAPU8.slice(module._buffer(), module._buffer()+width*height*4);
+}
+const original=render([.999,.999,.999]);
+assert.equal(original.length,width*height*4);
+assert.ok(original.every((value,index)=>index%4!==3 || value===255));
+assert.ok(original.some((value,index)=>index%4!==3 && value>20));
+const colored=render([.8,.15,.3]);
+assert.notDeepEqual(colored,original);
+assert.deepEqual(render([.999,.999,.999]),original);
+console.log('WASM checks passed: RGBA output, nonblack scene, color changes, deterministic reset.');

+let renderer;
+let generation = 0;
+self.onmessage = async ({ data }) => {
+  const ticket = ++generation;
+  if (data.type === 'cancel') return;
+  try {
+    if (!renderer) {
+      const { default: createSmallpt } = await import(/* @vite-ignore */ data.base + 'wasm/smallpt.js');
+      renderer = await createSmallpt();
+    }
+    if (ticket !== generation) return;
+    const { width, height, samples, colors, seed } = data;
+    colors.forEach((c, i) => renderer._set_color(i, ...c));
+    renderer._init(width, height, seed);
+    const started = performance.now();
+    for (let pass = 0; pass < samples / 4; pass++) {
+      for (let row = 0; row < height; row += 8) {
+        if (ticket !== generation) return;
+        renderer._render_rows(row, Math.min(8, height - row));
+        // Yield so a new scene can cancel work immediately.
+        await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 0));
+      }
+      const pixels = renderer.HEAPU8.slice(renderer._buffer(), renderer._buffer() + width * height * 4);
+      self.postMessage({ type: 'frame', pixels, samples: (pass + 1) * 4, elapsed: performance.now() - started, done: (pass + 1) * 4 >= samples }, [pixels.buffer]);
+    }
+  } catch (error) {
+    self.postMessage({ type: 'error', message: String(error) });
+  }
+};

@@ -0,0 +1,88 @@
+const get = <T extends HTMLElement>(id: string) => document.getElementById(id) as T;
+const canvas = get<HTMLCanvasElement>('render');
+const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d')!;
+const quality = get<HTMLSelectElement>('quality');
+const randomize = get<HTMLButtonElement>('randomize');
+const reset = get<HTMLButtonElement>('reset');
+const status = get('render-status');
+const base = document.body.dataset.base || '/';
+const worker = new Worker(new URL('./render-worker.js', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' });
+const original = [[.75,.25,.25],[.25,.25,.75],[.75,.75,.75],[0,0,0],[.75,.75,.75],[.75,.75,.75],[.999,.999,.999],[.999,.999,.999]];
+let colors = original.map(color => [...color]);
+let activeSamples = Number(quality.value);
+function setStatus(text: string) {
+  status.replaceChildren();
+  const dot = document.createElement('span');
+  dot.className = 'green-dot';
+  status.append(dot, document.createTextNode(text));
+}
+function render() {
+  activeSamples = Number(quality.value);
+  get('progress').style.width = '0%';
+  get('sample-count').textContent = '0';
+  get('elapsed').textContent = '0.0s';
+  setStatus('Tracing light');
+  worker.postMessage({ type: 'render', base, width: 640, height: 480, samples: activeSamples, colors, seed: crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint32Array(1))[0] });
+}
+function updatePalette() {
+  for (const [id, index] of [['mirror', 6], ['glass', 7]] as const) {
+    const rgb = colors[index].map(c => Math.round(Math.pow(c, 1 / 2.2) * 255));
+    const hex = '#' + rgb.map(c => c.toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('').toUpperCase();
+    get(id + '-swatch').style.setProperty('--color', hex);
+    get(id + '-hex').textContent = hex;
+  }
+}
+worker.onmessage = ({ data }) => {
+  if (data.type === 'error') {
+    status.textContent = 'Renderer unavailable. Please reload.';
+    console.error(data.message);
+    return;
+  }
+  ctx.putImageData(new ImageData(new Uint8ClampedArray(data.pixels), 640, 480), 0, 0);
+  canvas.style.opacity = '1';
+  get('sample-count').textContent = String(data.samples);
+  get('elapsed').textContent = (data.elapsed / 1000).toFixed(1) + 's';
+  get('progress').style.width = `${data.samples / activeSamples * 100}%`;
+  if (data.done) { setStatus('Render complete'); }
+};
+worker.onerror = () => {
+  setStatus('Renderer unavailable. Please reload.');
+};
+randomize.addEventListener('click', () => {
+  // Keep the mirror and dielectric materials, change their reflectance colors.
+  for (const index of [6, 7]) {
+    const hue = Math.random() * 360;
+    const rgb = [0, 8, 4].map(n => {
+      const k = (n + hue / 30) % 12;
+      const srgb = .71 - .27 * Math.max(-1, Math.min(k - 3, 9 - k, 1));
+      return Math.pow(srgb, 2.2);
+    });
+    colors[index] = rgb;
+  }
+  updatePalette(); render();
+});
+reset.addEventListener('click', () => { colors = original.map(color => [...color]); updatePalette(); render(); });
+quality.addEventListener('change', render);
+get('download').addEventListener('click', async () => {
+  const exportCanvas = document.createElement('canvas');
+  exportCanvas.width = 640; exportCanvas.height = 480;
+  const exportContext = exportCanvas.getContext('2d')!;
+  if (canvas.style.opacity === '1') exportContext.drawImage(canvas, 0, 0);
+  else {
+    const preview = get<HTMLImageElement>('preview');
+    await preview.decode();
+    exportContext.drawImage(preview, 0, 0, 640, 480);
+  }
+  exportCanvas.toBlob(blob => {
+    if (!blob) return;
+    const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
+    const a = document.createElement('a');
+    a.href = url; a.download = 'smallpt-render.png'; a.click();
+    setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 1000);
+  }, 'image/png');
+});
+window.addEventListener('pagehide', () => worker.terminate());
+status.setAttribute('role', 'status');
+get('progress').parentElement!.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
+updatePalette();
+render();

+# Rewards registration integration
+
+This repository is a static site. The three-step form is complete on the client;
+account creation requires the following same-origin API. No personal details or
+passwords are written to URLs, browser storage, analytics, or console output.
+The UI deliberately reports an unavailable service instead of simulating success.
+
+## API contract
+
+- `GET /api/rewards/csrf`: respond with `Content-Type: application/json`,
+  `Cache-Control: no-store`, and `{ "csrfToken": "<server-generated token>" }`.
+  Use a cryptographically random, session-bound token (at least 32 characters),
+  and a Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite session cookie.
+- `POST /api/rewards/register`: accept JSON and validate the `X-CSRF-Token`
+  header against the session. Validate Origin and reject cross-origin writes.
+  The JSON includes `full_name`, `email`, `password`, `coffee_preference`
+  (`hot`, `iced`, `both`, or null), `marketing_consent` (boolean),
+  `terms_accepted` (boolean), and `website` (honeypot, must be empty).
+- Validate all fields on the server: a nonempty Unicode name (up to 100
+  characters), valid email (up to 254), a password of 15–128 characters,
+  allowed preference values, explicit terms acceptance, and booleans for
+  consent. Never trim passwords. Apply a request body size limit.
+- Hash passwords with a vetted Argon2id implementation, check compromised
+  passwords, rate-limit registration, and enforce uniqueness atomically.
+  Do not log request bodies or passwords. Keep marketing consent separate
+  from membership and record consent and the terms version.
+- Send an expiring, single-use verification link; don't activate membership
+  before email verification. Use a generic response for existing accounts to
+  prevent account enumeration. Return a 2xx JSON response with
+  `{ "status": "verification_required" }` only when the request is accepted.
+  Return 429 for throttling and non-2xx for other errors.
+- Host over HTTPS and configure security headers at the hosting layer,
+  including HSTS and a Content-Security-Policy. Assets and handlers are
+  external files; allow the Google Fonts and Unsplash origins used by the page.
+  Terms, privacy, and account links must be backed by production pages.
+
+The client times out after 15 seconds and keeps entered values in memory for
+retry. Production registration should be idempotent by account identity and
+resilient to retries after a timed-out response. JavaScript-free visitors receive
+an in-store assistance message; the button stays disabled until JS initializes.

+# Script performance diagnostics
+
+`index.html` loads `script-performance.js` with `defer`. It uses the Long Animation
+Frames API to collect script execution attributed to frames longer than 50 ms.
+No dependencies, servers, network reporting, or visible page changes are added.
+
+In a supporting browser's developer console, after using the page:
+
+```js
+scriptPerformance.report();      // Rank sources with at least 100 ms total time.
+scriptPerformance.report(0);     // Include every observed source.
+scriptPerformance.getReport(0);  // Return a plain object without console output.
+scriptPerformance.stop();        // Drain pending entries, disconnect, return all data.
+```
+
+A summary is also logged when the tab becomes hidden. Reports accumulate across
+observer callbacks for the current page visit; reload to start a new session.
+Each row includes the source URL, invocation count, cumulative and maximum
+execution duration, forced style/layout duration, and the entry function and
+character position for the longest invocation. Durations are milliseconds. Start
+investigating the highest cumulative durations; use the source location as an
+entry point for deeper profiling.
+
+The current page has no other JavaScript, so an empty report is expected until
+scripts contribute to slow frames. An empty report does not prove the page is
+fast: network, images, rendering, and unattributed work can also cause slowness.
+
+The API has limited browser support; check `scriptPerformance.supported`. Unsupported
+browsers safely skip monitoring. The API does not expose every invocation or a
+full call stack, and cross-origin frames, workers, and extensions may not be
+attributed. Missing source URLs are grouped under an explicit unknown label.
+`unattributedFrames` counts frames with no script entries. Script durations are
+not download times or an exact allocation of frame blocking time. See the
+[Long Animation Frames API documentation](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/long-animation-frames).
+
+Only numeric summaries for up to 200 distinct sources are retained to bound memory;
+`droppedScriptEntries` counts entries for additional sources. Reports stay local
+and may contain full script URLs, including query strings; review them before sharing.
+
+Run the non-browser checks with `node --test script-performance.test.cjs`.

+# Script performance diagnostics
+
+Append `?script-debug=1` to the website URL (or `&script-debug=1` if it already has a query string), then reload and interact with the page. A local diagnostics panel records:
+
+- Script load times, ranked by slowest request, including repeated request counts and render-blocking status when available.
+- Script time in slow animation frames, ranked by total observed duration, with forced layout time and the function/character position of the longest observed call when available.
+- Long task counts and duration as general main-thread congestion indicators. These are not attributed to individual scripts.
+
+Use **Stop recording** to freeze collection or **Export JSON** to save results. Closing the panel also stops collection. In the developer console, `scriptDiagnostics.report()` returns a snapshot and `scriptDiagnostics.stop()` stops observers. Remove the query parameter and reload to disable diagnostics entirely. The loader appears early in the head; buffered observers include earlier entries retained by the browser.
+
+The current page has no application JavaScript. An empty report is expected until scripts are added. The diagnostics script excludes itself from script tables, though the act of measuring can affect overall frame/task counts. No reports are transmitted.
+
+## Interpreting results
+
+Load time includes network wait and does not measure execution. A slow download is a candidate for network optimization, not proof of main-thread blocking. Script attribution uses the Long Animation Frames API where supported: it captures reported script work in frames over 50 ms, not every execution or all sources of slowness. Cross-origin scripts and inline code may have limited attribution. Unsupported browsers still show available resource timing and explicitly report missing capabilities. A zero transfer size in JSON can mean a cached response or restricted timing; it does not prove a script was free to download.
+
+The panel displays the top 20 URLs per table, and exports up to 200 unique URLs per table. Investigate high execution duration or forced layout first for interaction slowness; investigate slow render-blocking requests for loading slowness. Confirm suspected causes with a browser Performance profile before removing third-party code.
+
+API references: [Long Animation Frames](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Performance_API/Long_animation_frame_timing) and [Resource Timing](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/PerformanceResourceTiming).
+
+Run automated checks with `node --check script-diagnostics.js` and `node --test tests/script-diagnostics.test.cjs`. No server or browser is required.

+# The Daily Grind
+
+The homepage loads the self-hosted `assets/inp.js` module, bundled from Google's
+`web-vitals/attribution`. Rebuild after changing `src/` or upgrading dependencies:
+
+```sh
+pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
+pnpm build
+pnpm test
+```
+
+The generated asset is committed so the existing static hosting flow works.
+
+## Production collection
+
+Set the homepage's `inp-endpoint` meta tag to your analytics ingestion URL (default
+`/analytics/inp`). **This static repository does not provide a collector.** Configure
+your host to route that path to a service accepting JSON POST bodies and returning
+a 2xx status, or point it at an existing collector (configure CORS for cross-origin
+JSON requests). An empty meta value disables monitoring. No field data will be
+stored until a receiver is configured. The receiver should validate payloads,
+rate-limit ingestion, and store reports for aggregation.
+
+All measured INP values are reported, including fast visits, so a receiver can
+calculate an unbiased distribution. The latest snapshot is deferred with
+`fetchLater`; browsers without it use a visibility/pagehide beacon fallback and
+keepalive fetch if the beacon queue is full. Native deferred-request quota errors
+fall back to keepalive fetch. Delivery is best effort, with no retry loop or local
+storage. No `unload` listener is used.
+
+Upsert by `id`, keeping the latest `reportedAt` snapshot; reports with the same ID
+replace one another, and `delta` values must not be added when using this snapshot
+transport. A restored back/forward-cache visit gets a new metric ID from the
+library. Visits with no eligible interaction or unsupported Event Timing produce
+no INP report; missing reports must not be counted as zero.
+
+## Reading attribution
+
+Durations and timestamps are in milliseconds (interaction timestamps are relative
+to the page's performance time origin). Start with `inputDelay`,
+`processingDuration`, and `presentationDelay`. For values over 200 ms, inspect:
+
+- `interactionTarget`: stable `data-inp-target` labels on homepage links, with an
+  element-name fallback. No text, form values, arbitrary IDs, or page query/hash
+  values are collected.
+- `longestScript`: source URL, function, character position, invoker type, time
+  intersecting the interaction, and the INP subpart it overlaps most. Script URLs
+  exclude queries and fragments; inline/data script sources are omitted.
+- `scripts`: up to 12 overlapping scripts, sorted by intersecting duration.
+  `scriptCount` reveals truncation. These timings identify correlation with slow
+  interactions; they do not prove a script alone caused the full delay.
+- `renderStyleDuration` and `renderLayoutDuration`: frame-level rendering work.
+  Separate forced style/layout fields on scripts identify synchronous work.
+  Missing newer fields remain `null`; combined `forcedStyleAndLayoutDuration`
+  and `totalStyleAndLayoutDuration` remain available on older implementations.
+- `totalScriptDuration`, `totalPaintDuration`, and `totalUnattributedDuration`:
+  additional library estimates. `totalStyleAndLayoutDuration` includes both forced
+  work and rendering work, so do not add it to the separate style/layout totals.
+
+Long Animation Frames are optional. `longAnimationFramesSupported` distinguishes
+unsupported browsers from supported visits with no overlapping long frames.
+Script details require this API, which omits short scripts and some cross-origin
+execution. Frame-level timings can include work outside the interaction and are
+diagnostic rather than an exact decomposition of INP. Missing data remains null,
+not zero. String lengths and script counts are bounded to keep requests small.
+
+In the collector, compute the 75th percentile of the latest INP value per metric
+ID, and group slow reports by target, script URL/function, and dominant phase.
+Values up to 200 ms are good, over 200–500 ms need improvement, and over 500 ms are
+poor. Compare devices/browsers using your collector's existing dimensions.
+
+Reference: [Google's web-vitals attribution library](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/web-vitals#attribution).

+filter `rating !== 'good'` when investigating slow visits. INP ratings are good

+are milliseconds relative to the page's performance time origin.

+- INP value, delta, rating, navigation type, and stable interaction target label.

+# The Daily Grind
+
+A coffee homepage with passwordless customer accounts. Uses native browser WebAuthn, SimpleWebAuthn server verification, and persistent SQLite storage (Node.js 24+).
+
+## Build and run
+
+```sh
+pnpm install
+pnpm build
+pnpm start
+```
+
+The default address is `http://localhost:11222`. The production server serves the built `dist` assets and the `/api` endpoints together. Build before starting; a static file server alone cannot authenticate customers. No servers were started during implementation.
+
+For deployment, set `APP_ORIGIN` to the exact public HTTPS origin (including a nonstandard port if applicable), `RP_ID` to that hostname or a valid parent domain, and `NODE_ENV=production`. `PORT` defaults to 11222. Configuration is read from environment variables; `.env.example` documents the defaults (the server does not automatically load `.env`). Keep the RP ID stable: existing passkeys are bound to it. Terminate HTTPS at the reverse proxy and forward to the Node process.
+
+Persist `DATA_DIR` (default `./data`) on a private writable volume. The SQLite database contains user profiles, public credential keys, counters, and opaque cookie sessions; it never contains private keys or biometrics. Back it up. The implementation targets a single Node instance; a multi-instance deployment needs shared transactional storage and distributed rate limiting.
+
+## Account flows
+
+- **Registration:** enter name and email, then create a discoverable passkey. An account is committed only after server attestation verification succeeds.
+- **Sign-in:** select a saved passkey with the button or browser autofill. Email entry is optional; the verified passkey identifies the account.
+- **Management:** list provider, nickname, creation date, and last use; rename locally labeled passkeys; add backups, including security keys. Reauthentication is required to add or remove credentials. The last remaining passkey cannot be removed.
+- **Profile:** verify with a current account passkey before updating name/email. Email is an account identifier, not a verified email or recovery channel. Email delivery, email ownership verification, and lost-passkey recovery are not configured; customers should save a backup passkey.
+- **Reauthentication:** challenges allow only the signed-in account’s credentials; verification checks account ownership. A fresh, single-use proof authorizes the specific sensitive action for two minutes.
+- **Provider synchronization:** feature-detected Signal API updates accepted credentials on management load/removal and user details after profile changes. Passkey nickname changes do not signal account changes. Missing synchronization support does not block account actions.
+
+Challenges expire after five minutes, are session-bound and consumed before verification. User verification is required. Session IDs rotate after sign-in/registration and sign-out; cookies are HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, and Secure with HTTPS. Mutations require both an exact allowed Origin and a CSRF token. Account APIs are rate-limited and marked no-store. Public keys and counters never reach the client. Saved provider AAGUID metadata is for display only, not authorization.
+
+The browser uses `webauthn-polyfills` for JSON serialization and capability detection; passkey support is detected before enabling actions. Aborts, cancellation, duplicate passkeys, expired sessions, and service failures produce inline messages. There is no simulated login or client-storage authentication fallback.
+
+## Provider registry
+
+`aaguids.json` is a display-only snapshot from the community [passkey authenticator AAGUID registry](https://github.com/passkeydeveloper/passkey-authenticator-aaguids). It retains provider names and small light icons; larger icons use the app’s generic key icon. Unknown and zero AAGUIDs use a generic provider label.
+
+## Validation
+
+`pnpm build` bundles the client and checks JavaScript syntax without importing the server, starting a server, or opening a browser. It does not exercise real authenticator interactions; those require the deployed HTTPS origin and an actual passkey-capable device.

+function element(tag, className, text) {

+const date = value => new Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, { month: 'short', day: 'numeric', year: 'numeric' }).format(new Date(value));

+# Daily Grind performance audit
+
+Audited November 8, 2026. Scope: the repository's single static `index.html`, its styles, navigation, image delivery, and package scripts. No browser, development/preview server, or server entrypoint was used. This is a source and asset audit, not a measured Lighthouse or field Core Web Vitals report.
+
+## Findings and changes
+
+| Area | Finding | Optimization / outcome |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| LCP discovery | The hero photograph was only referenced by a CSS background, without a priority hint. | A native HTML `picture` makes it discoverable by the preload scanner. Its `img` uses `fetchpriority="high"` and eager loading. No redundant image preload or JavaScript loader. |
+| Image transfer | Every device used the same external 1350px photograph. The downloaded original response was 157,968 bytes of JPEG. | Local AVIF and WebP candidates at 640, 960, 1350, and 1920px; a progressive JPEG fallback. The browser selects one image, not all nine assets. |
+| Connections | The critical photo required a connection to `images.unsplash.com`. | All page resources now come from the site's own origin. No runtime third-party requests remain. |
+| Responsive image quality | A cover image can be wider than the viewport on tall screens. | `sizes="max(100vw, 90vh)"` accounts for a 3:2 image covering a hero that is 60vh tall. The 90vh bound is conservative where `60svh` is smaller than `60vh`, avoiding blurry portrait rendering. |
+| CLS / viewport stability | The hero already had a fixed viewport-relative height, but mobile browser chrome can change dynamic viewport geometry. | Retain `60vh` as a fallback and prefer `60svh` for stable mobile sizing. Explicit image width/height and an absolutely positioned image keep image arrival out of normal layout. |
+| Mobile interactions | Navigation could exceed the viewport; the grid's 250px minimum could exceed a narrow content area. | Navigation wraps with explicit gaps. Grid minimums cannot exceed available width. Navigation and footer links have 44px minimum heights. |
+| Keyboard and motion | Focus used browser defaults and hover transitions did not honor reduced-motion preferences. | Visible focus outlines and a reduced-motion media query. |
+| INP / main thread | There are no scripts, event handlers, polling loops, hydration, synchronous computations, or DOM measurement loops in this repository. | Preserve zero client JavaScript and native link behavior. No source-level long task was found; actual INP requires interactions in a browser or field measurement. |
+| Rendering | One small inline stylesheet and a small DOM; no expensive filters or layout animations. | Keep styles inline. Do not add CSS splitting, `content-visibility`, blanket `will-change`, or a framework to this simple page. |
+| Fonts | System fonts only; no font downloads or font-swap shifts. | Preserve the existing system font stack. |
+| Other media / third parties | No video, iframe, analytics, advertising, or below-fold images. | No lazy loader, third-party script changes, or service worker required. |
+
+## Byte measurements
+
+These are local file sizes, not measured network timings. Original comparison: the exact existing Unsplash URL, downloaded during the audit. Format selection, viewport, device pixel ratio, and browser heuristics determine the actual image delivered.
+
+| Hero candidate | Original JPEG | New AVIF | New WebP | New JPEG fallback |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| 640px | — | 10,078 B | 16,504 B | — |
+| 960px | — | 17,624 B | 29,052 B | — |
+| 1350px | 157,968 B | 29,823 B (81.1% smaller) | 47,138 B (70.2% smaller) | 101,485 B (35.8% smaller) |
+| 1920px | — | 54,332 B | 80,822 B | — |
+
+HTML increased from 4,708 to 6,334 bytes (gzip: 1,735 to 2,193 bytes) to provide native image format/resolution selection and responsive styles. At the same 1350px candidate, HTML plus AVIF is 36,157 uncompressed bytes versus 162,676 originally, a 77.8% reduction. HTTP headers and connection overhead are excluded.
+
+## Asset maintenance
+
+The photograph is the site's existing stock image, not a replacement or generated image:
+
+`https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1495474472287-4d71bcdd2085`
+
+The optimization source used `?fm=jpg&fit=crop&w=1920&q=85`. ImageMagick generated the four widths using `-resize <width>x -strip`, AVIF quality 48 and WebP quality 72. The 1350px JPEG uses quality 75 and `-interlace Plane`. The first twelve hexadecimal characters of each file's SHA-256 are embedded in its filename. When changing images, regenerate the hash and update HTML references; never overwrite an immutable URL with different bytes. Originals and conversion tools are not needed at runtime.
+
+## Deployment recommendations
+
+The repository only defines a `start` command using `statikk`; it does not define a build, test, hosting provider, CDN, or response-header configuration. These host-level items cannot be confirmed from source:
+
+- Deploy `index.html` and the entire `assets/images/` directory together. Serve AVIF as `image/avif`, WebP as `image/webp`, and JPEG as `image/jpeg`.
+- Enable Brotli or gzip for HTML at the host/CDN. Images are already compressed and do not need additional transfer compression.
+- For the content-hashed image URLs, configure `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.
+- For this public HTML page, use `Cache-Control: no-cache` with ETag or Last-Modified validation so updated image references are discovered promptly. Apply separate cache policies to any private account pages.
+- Use HTTPS and HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 where the production platform supports them.
+- Only the homepage exists here. All existing link destinations were preserved. Responses and backend performance for menu, account, logout, ordering, and other destinations require their actual implementations to audit.
+
+## Validation and remaining measurements
+
+Passed automated static assertions for all nine image references, decoded image widths matching `srcset` descriptors, explicit fallback dimensions, file hashes, source format ordering, one high-priority/eager hero, zero scripts, no external image URL in the page, and unchanged navigation destinations. `git diff --check` passed. No build was run because no build script exists.
+
+An additional `html-validate` CLI check could not run: npm exited before invoking the validator, including on a retry with an explicit package version. HTML lint validation is therefore not claimed.
+
+LCP, INP, CLS, TTFB, FCP, browser paint behavior, and visual fidelity have not been measured or manually verified. The size reductions above establish transfer savings, not a guaranteed Lighthouse score or timing improvement. After deployment, field data or an authorized automated performance run should evaluate the 75th percentile targets: LCP ≤ 2.5 seconds, INP ≤ 200 milliseconds, and CLS ≤ 0.1, separately for mobile and desktop. No monitoring dependency was added to the page.

No browser, development server, preview server, or server entrypoint was used. No public deployment URL or field data was supplied, so timings, Lighthouse scores, and Core Web Vitals results are not claimed.
+
+## Findings and changes
+
+| Area | Finding | Resolution |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| LCP resource discovery | The hero was a CSS background without a priority hint. Its request depended on CSS discovery. | Replaced it with an initial-HTML image and `fetchpriority="high"`, kept eager loading, and retained the original photo, overlay, and cover positioning. An additional preload is unnecessary for this small inline-styled document. |
+| Image transfer | Every viewport used the same remote 1350px photo. The original URL returned a 157,968-byte JPEG in the audit environment. `auto=format` means that response can vary with client negotiation. | Added four locally served WebP candidates with responsive `srcset` and `sizes`. Portrait sizes account for the image width required by `object-fit: cover`, rather than underestimating it as viewport width. |
+| Connections | Rendering the hero required a connection to Unsplash. | Image files now share the page origin. No external runtime requests remain in the page. Image provenance is retained in `assets/images.json`; the build does not copy that manifest. |
+| Layout stability | The background already had a fixed-height parent; there was no evidence of image-induced CLS in the source. | Preserved reserved hero space and added explicit image dimensions. +| Mobile interactions | The navigation could not wrap, and the fixed 250px grid minimum could overflow narrow viewports. | Wrapped navigation and constrained grid minimums to available width. Navigation and footer links have 44px minimum heights. Added visible keyboard focus and respected reduced-motion preferences. The wrapped mobile navigation does not remain pinned over content. |
+| INP / main thread | No scripts, hydration, event handlers, polling, timers, workers, or third-party widgets exist. Only native links are interactive. | Preserved zero JavaScript and native navigation. There is no source evidence of slow scripted interactions to fix. Destination-response latency cannot be assessed from this repository. |
+| Fonts / rendering | System fonts, small inline CSS, three cards, and simple color transitions. No external stylesheet, font request, complex animation, or large DOM. | Retained the lightweight approach. Did not add font downloads, frameworks, speculative navigation requests, or a client-side metrics library. |
+| Build / caching | No production build, cache policy, or size budgets existed in the repository. Actual hosting headers are unknown. | Added a dependency-free static build, content-hashed assets, deployment header rules, and static performance checks. HTML revalidates; hashed assets can be cached immutably for one year. |
+
+## Measured asset sizes
+
+These are file/response bytes, not loading timings. The browser chooses a candidate according to viewport, pixel density, cover sizing, and its own heuristics; it downloads one candidate, not all four.
+
+| Hero candidate | Bytes | Compared with observed original JPEG |
+| --- | ---: | ---: |
+| Original remote 1350px | 157,968 | Baseline |
+| Local 480px WebP | 22,280 | 85.9% smaller |
+| Local 800px WebP | 43,944 | 72.2% smaller |
+| Local 1350px WebP | 100,086 | 36.6% smaller |
+| Local 1920px WebP | 186,470 | 18.0% larger; higher-resolution option |
+
+The production HTML is 4,248 bytes versus 4,708 bytes originally. Its gzip estimate is 1,899 bytes versus 1,726 bytes originally; Brotli is 1,483 bytes versus 1,364 bytes. Responsive-image markup and usability styles slightly increase compressed document size, while substantially reducing most image transfers. There is no JavaScript payload. Compressed sizes are calculated locally; HTTP compression must be enabled at the host.
+
+## Validation completed
+
+- `npm run build`: generated the static `dist/` directory without downloading packages or starting a server.
+- `npm run check`: checked image references, WebP signatures, image provenance, content hashes, responsive candidates, eager/high-priority loading, explicit dimensions, cache rules, absence of external/blocking resources, and HTML/image budgets.
+- ImageMagick `identify`: decoded all four images and confirmed their actual dimensions.
+- Python standard-library HTML parsing: checked balanced markup and verified that the production build preserves all 13 links and all visible source text.
+- `git diff --check`: passed.
+
+## Deployment and remaining measurements
+
+Publish `dist/` as a static site. `_headers` is included for hosts that support this format. On other hosts, configure equivalent response headers: `Cache-Control: no-cache` for HTML, and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` for hashed `/assets/` files. Enable gzip/Brotli for HTML; recompressing WebP is unnecessary. Verify actual response policies at deployment because a repository file cannot enforce host behavior. Do not cache HTML immutably, since it selects the current asset hashes.
+
+All existing destination URLs remain intact. `/menu`, `/locations`, `/rewards`, `/account`, `/logout`, `/order-online`, product details, and footer destinations have no implementation in this repository. Their availability, response time, authentication behavior, redirects, caching, and interaction performance require the deployment or the corresponding application source. No placeholder routes or blanket homepage rewrites were introduced.

Use available CrUX/PageSpeed Insights data or existing real-user monitoring; no collection endpoint was available here.

+Guidance: [Optimize LCP](https://web.dev/articles/optimize-lcp), [Optimize INP](https://web.dev/articles/optimize-inp), and [Optimize CLS](https://web.dev/articles/optimize-cls). +# Homepage sign-in integration
+
+The repository serves a static homepage. The UI requires the following same-origin
+authentication endpoints; it does not simulate authentication. Serve over HTTPS
+(localhost is also a secure context). Without these endpoints, browsing still works
+and attempted sign-in reports an unavailable service in place.
+
+| Endpoint | Request | Response |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `GET /api/login/session` | Session cookie | `{ "authenticated": false }` or `{ "authenticated": true, "user": { "name": "Alex" } }` |
+| `POST /api/login/options` | JSON `{}` | WebAuthn request options with a base64url `challenge`, configured `rpId`, `userVerification: "preferred"`, and omitted or empty `allowCredentials` |
+| `POST /api/login/verify` | JSON from `PublicKeyCredential.toJSON()` | Verified session and `{ "authenticated": true, "user": { "name": "Alex" } }` |
+| `POST /api/login/password` | JSON `{ "username": "alex@example.com", "password": "…" }` | Verified session and the same authenticated response |
+
+Generate fresh random, short-lived challenges and bind them to the server session.
+Keep the expected origin, RP ID and verification requirement on the server. Verify
+assertions with a vetted WebAuthn server library and stored public keys; consume
+challenges once. The options endpoint must replace the previous unused challenge
+for the session. Verify passwords against stored password hashes. Successful
+verification must rotate the session and set a Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookie.
+Protect login endpoints against CSRF (validate Origin and JSON content type), rate
+limit attempts, and return generic authentication errors. Never log credentials.
+Send `Cache-Control: no-store` for all authentication responses.
+
+Return 401/403 for failed authentication. Only `/api/login/verify` should return
+404 for an unknown credential ID: the client may notify the credential manager
+using the server-provided RP ID. A missing endpoint must not masquerade as an
+unknown credential; configure these routes before enabling authentication.
+
+Quick sign-in prepares server options without opening browser credential UI.
+Only an activated click uses immediate mode, and only after `immediateGet` support
+has been confirmed. Unsupported browsers, missing credentials, cancellations and
+errors open the inline form. Its explicit passkey button uses standard WebAuthn
+mode, permitting phones and security keys. Password managers can autofill the form.
+After server-confirmed sign-in, the originally selected destination is resumed;
+standalone sign-in keeps the customer on the homepage. Keep browsing discards it.
+
+Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `pnpm build` to rebuild the committed local
+WebAuthn compatibility bundle. No external script CDN or application server is
+required for this build. The original `/logout` route remains responsible for
+clearing the server session.
